title: Proposal: agent-discoverable page metadata

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
## Problem

AI agents are a primary consumer of HTML pages now. When an agent lands on a page, it needs to know:

- What does this page *do*?
- What actions are available?
- Is there a structured API or markdown version?

Today agents reverse-engineer this from DOM structure, `<title>`, OG tags, and Schema.org JSON-LD — all designed for humans or search crawlers, not for agents that need to **act**.

## What's missing

| Mechanism | What it tells agents |
|-----------|---------------------|
| `<meta name="description">` | Marketing copy. Not useful. |
| Open Graph | Social card data. Not actionable. |
| Schema.org JSON-LD | Good for entities, poor for *actions* |
| `robots.txt` | What *not* to do, not what *can* be done |
| `llms.txt` | Site-level, not page-level. Not HTML. |

None of these say: "this page lets you search products and add them to a cart — here's the API endpoint."

## Proposal

Three additions using existing HTML patterns (`<meta name>`, `<link rel>`). No new elements, no custom namespaces.

### 1. Page purpose for agents

```html
<meta name="agent-description" 
      content="Product listing. Supports search, filter by category/price, add to cart.">
<meta name="agent-actions" content="search, filter, add-to-cart, compare">
```

`agent-description` is factual — what the page *does*. Not what it's *about*.

`agent-actions` — an agent reading `<head>` instantly knows whether this page is worth engaging with for a given task.

### 2. Machine-readable alternatives

```html
<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown" href="/products.md">
<link rel="alternate" type="application/json" href="/api/v1/products">
<link rel="agent-api" type="application/mcp" href="/mcp">
```

`rel="alternate"` already exists. The new `rel="agent-api"` signals: "this URL lets agents *do things*, not just read."

### 3. Full example

```html
<head>
  <!-- Human-oriented (unchanged) -->
  <meta name="description" content="Premium wireless headphones. Free shipping!">
  
  <!-- Agent-oriented (proposed) -->
  <meta name="agent-description" 
        content="Product detail for SKU WH-400. Price, specs, reviews, stock. Supports add-to-cart.">
  <meta name="agent-actions" content="add-to-cart, add-to-wishlist, check-stock">
  <link rel="alternate" type="application/json" href="/api/v1/products/wh-400">
  <link rel="agent-api" type="application/mcp" href="/mcp">
</head>
```

Agent reads `<head>`, knows what it can do, hits the API or MCP endpoint. Falls back to DOM parsing only if none of this exists.

## How this differs from prior proposals

- **#11548** (`llms:*` meta tags) — used a non-standard namespace, was LLM-specific. This uses standard `<meta name>` and `<link rel>`, works for any agent.
- **#9334** (`ai-consent`) — about training data policy, not discoverability.
- **#10946** (`aid-markup`) — per-element attributes, much larger surface. This is `<head>`-only.

## Prior art

- [WebMCP](https://github.com/webmachinelearning/webmcp) `navigator.modelContext` — runtime JS API for tools; this covers the static HTML discovery layer
- [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org/) — site-level; this is page-level
- [A2A Agent Cards](https://github.com/google/a2a-spec) — agent-to-agent; this is page-to-agent
- [Schema.org Actions](https://schema.org/Action) — entity-level in JSON-LD; this is a simpler `<meta>` signal
- [ARD `ai-catalog.json`](https://agenticresourcediscovery.org/) — domain-level index; this is page-level

## Open questions

1. Should `agent-actions` be a comma list or structured JSON?
2. Is `rel="agent-api"` the right name? Alternatives: `rel="agent-tools"`, `rel="agent-service"`
3. Should there be a controlled vocabulary for page types, or is free text fine?
4. How does this interact with WebMCP's `navigator.modelContext`?

---

I've been building in this space — [WebMCP bridge proposals](https://github.com/webmachinelearning/webmcp/issues/83), [browser AI apps](https://h3manth.com/ai/eloquent/), [MCP servers](https://github.com/hemanth/tc39-mcp) — and the lack of page-level agent metadata is a consistent friction point.
